I have been thinking a lot about Wait Calculations. Especially in mathematics and biology, there is high likelihood that models now in development can make serious gains (with or without human help) on hard problems.

The strawberry thing was very funny but probably gave people the wrong impression of where AI was heading in math.

I suspect we will see more of this across fields and professions that will increasingly be forced to help people understand that their jobs consist not only the most visible tasks that AI can do, but also tasks that the AI cannot do or does badly.

AI can discover superhuman proofs, but that is not all that the math profession is about, and actually can undermine and reduce the attention to the other aspects of the job that are important to mathematicians. It becomes harder to defend the value of the many other tasks mathematicians do
Kind of expecting to see a stance on here where people argue both that AI is fake & not capable of doing anything interesting and also that it presents an existential threat.
